# hvir

Desktop developer workbench for local and SSH projects. It combines a native terminal, Git and worktree workflows, file viewing and document review, and launch profiles for coding-agent harnesses.

hvir is an Electron app (React renderer, Node main process). Terminals run through `node-pty` and [ghostty-web](https://github.com/jarmak-personal/ghostty-web). Bundled harness providers include a plain shell, Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and custom commands.

## Requirements

- Node.js 24 or newer
- npm
- A C/C++ toolchain for native modules (`node-pty`, `@hvir/rename-noreplace`)
- macOS or Linux for packaged builds (macOS `.pkg`, Linux `.deb`)

`postinstall` rebuilds native modules against Electron. On a fresh clone that step needs the same toolchain used to compile Node addons.

## Develop

```sh
npm install
npm run dev
```

Other day-to-day commands:

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run build` | Typecheck and production build |
| `npm run preview` | Preview the production renderer build |
| `npm test` | Unit tests (Vitest) |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint |
| `npm run format` | Prettier write |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc` for the Node and web projects |
| `npm run verify` | Architecture checks, lint, typecheck, and tests |
| `npm run smoke` | Build the smoke app and run the scenario suite |
| `npm run hooks:install` | Install the repo git hooks |

`npm run smoke:scenario <name>` runs one smoke scenario after a smoke build. See `package.json` for the full scenario list used by `npm run smoke`.

## Layout

- `src/main` — Electron main process: projects, PTY, Git, SSH hosts, windows, IPC
- `src/preload` — renderer bridge
- `src/renderer` — React workbench UI
- `src/shared` — IPC and domain types shared by main and renderer
- `src/workers` — utility and Git workers
- `packages/rename-noreplace` — optional native rename helper
- `scripts` — smoke, release, architecture, and project-management tooling
- `test` — Vitest suites and fixtures

## Package

```sh
npm run pack:mac:arm64
npm run pack:linux:x64
npm run pack:linux:arm64
```

Artifacts are written under `dist/`. Signing is opt-in via `npm run pack:mac:arm64:signed`. Do not commit signing secrets.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party notices shipped with the app are in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
